newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka party says MP should report to police.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka party says MP should report to police.

text.p: The leader of Sri Lanka's main opposition United National Party said on Thursday a UNP legislator sought in connection with the killing of a ruling coalition member of parliament should report to police.
"We have asked MP Susantha Punchinilame (and others) to give themselves up to the police," former prime minister Ranil Wickremesinghe told a news conference.

Nalanda Ellawala, 29, member of parliament from the ruling People's Alliance, was killed by unknown gunmen on Tuesday during a roadside quarrel between his supporters and UNP rivals in Kuruwita, a town in Ratnapura district, 80 km (50 miles) southeast of Colombo.

The killing occurred on the eve of the deadline for filing nominations for the March 21 local polls, the first electoral test for President Chandrika Kumaratunga's coalition People's Alliance government.
The alliance toppled the UNP from 17 years in power in 1994.

The polls are for local assemblies and mayors in seven of the country's nine provinces. The government scrapped polls in the northern and eastern provinces because of guerrilla activity by separatist Tamils.

Police on Wednesday said they were searching for Punchinilame, his bodyguard and the former mayor of Ratnapura city, Mahinda Ratnatilleke, for questioning in connection with the case. No arrest warrants have been issued.
Wickremesinghe said he had advised Punchinilame to seek the advice of lawyers when he telephoned him soon after the incident on Tuesday. He said he had had no contact with him since then.

"Any UNP member found guilty in this incident will be expelled from the party," Wickremesinghe said. He said his party's Working Committee would meet on Friday to decide what course of action the party should take.
"We condemn these killings," he said. "Let the guilty be punished. There's been too much violence in this country. The UNP has denounced the culture of political violence."
Wickremesinghe also said UNP supporters in Ratnapura had been attacked and several homes and shops set on fire by mobs after the killing.
"We're going to face this election come what may, whatever the conditions, and we'll win," Wickremesinghe said.
